To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clinical champions in acute care are a heterogeneous group of individuals who have a wide range of roles, responsibilities, and motivations.

the clinical champions in the acute care settings we studied were motivated by a strong sense of professional identity, a desire to provide the best possible patient care and to make a difference in patients' lives, and a commitment to improving the quality of care.

clinical champions across the three levels of acute healthcare are: (i) motivated by a desire to improve the quality of care and the patient experience; (ii) committed to the implementation of evidence into practice and to supporting other clinicians; and (iii) are often supported by their colleagues and managers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the clinical champion in the implementation of clinical guidelines.
the development of a theoretical understanding of the clinical champions role, in the context of acute care, as well as an empirical understanding of the role in practice.
the role of clinical champions in the adoption of evidence-based practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clinical champions in acute care settings can be found across three levels of clinical care, namely at the bedside, in the ward and at the hospital level.
the clinical champion is a key player in the implementation of change.
the role of the clinical champion is a complex one and that it can be difficult to define and describe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for clinical champions that is based on the work of other researchers and our own experiences and observations.
the role of clinical champions is complex, with the potential for significant positive and negative impacts on the quality of patient care.
clinical champions are important to the success of the implementation of a new practice or technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

clinical champions are not just individuals but are also embedded in the context of a hospital, and that the context in which clinical champions operate is important in understanding their roles, their actions and their impact.
clinical champions have a significant influence on the success of implementation.
clinical champions can be effective in improving care, but they must be supported by the right people and the right systems.
